title: Driven-dissipative superconductivity in moiré heterostructure without attraction
authors: Tsung-Sheng Huang, Atac Imamoglu, Mohammad Hafezi, Sebastian Diehl
abstract: Dissipative preparation of quantum order offers a route to superconductivity that does not rely on enhancing attractive interactions. Here we propose a driven-dissipative protocol to prepare superconductivity as a stationary state of a two-dimensional moiré heterostructure. The key ingredient is a bilayer moiré platform in which the layer degree of freedom acts as a pseudospin, allowing the pseudospin structure required for pairing to be implemented through optically induced spatial operations. This preparation scheme requires local dissipation, which we show to arises naturally from weakly dispersive bosonic modes in the heterostructure. In contrast, in the opposite regime of collective dissipation, the same platform exhibits an early-time superradiant burst. Our results establish driven-dissipative moiré heterostructures as a promising platform for preparing superconductivity, while also revealing a connection between steady-state pairing and transient superradiance.
summary: The paper introduces a method to engineer superconductivity in moiré heterostructures purely through controlled dissipation, bypassing the need for attractive interactions. By modeling the system dynamics using Lindblad master equations derived from coupling to bosonic modes, they show that local dissipation naturally drives the system into a BCS superconducting steady state. This establishes a powerful theoretical framework connecting non-equilibrium physics with fundamental quantum phenomena.
main_problem: The authors propose a novel mechanism to achieve superconductivity (SC) as a stationary state without relying on enhancing attractive interactions.
main_result: They demonstrate that engineered local dissipation in moiré heterostructures can drive the system into a BCS superconducting state, establishing this platform as promising for SC preparation.
method: The analysis uses Lindblad master equations derived through systematic approximations like adiabatic elimination and Born-Markov assumptions to model open quantum systems dynamics.
model_or_system: The physical system is a two-dimensional moiré heterostructure, specifically utilizing a bilayer platform where layer pseudospins control pairing. The dynamics are governed by a Lindblad master equation incorporating coupling to bosonic modes (HPPs).
key_observables: Superconducting gap/BCS state formation, transient superradiant bursts, and coherence/incoherence couplings J(R) and $\Upsilon$(R).
important_parameters: The ratio of electronic orbital width to moiré lattice constant ($a_W/a_M$), and the relative strengths of driving fields vs. dissipation rates.
main_assumptions: Key approximations include adiabatic elimination of auxiliary lattices/conduction electrons, Born-Markov approximation for bath integration, and assuming specific small parameter hierarchies for validity.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the moiré heterostructure setup, the engineered dissipation process involving Raman transitions, and numerical confirmations of local dissipation conditions ($\Upsilon(\mathbf{R}) \sim \delta_{\mathbf{R},0}$).
paper_structure: The paper builds from defining the general driven-dissipative framework using Lindblad equations to deriving effective Hamiltonians via polaron transformations and adiabatic elimination, culminating in the final master equation describing SC formation and superradiance.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it merges concepts from open quantum systems (dissipation engineering) with condensed matter physics (superconductivity), providing a concrete platform for studying non-equilibrium quantum phases.
